brief.headline: Cut the 30mm measuring-cup price by 8% to match Premier Plastic, then switch payment to 30 days and free up ₹10.19 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Drop the 30mm measuring cup from ₹0.38/NOS to ₹0.35/NOS
priceAsk.basis: Premier Plastic sells us the same cup at ₹0.35/NOS; Mars is 8.6% higher. The market asking price for a similar 28mm PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typically ₹0.85–0.95), and the verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so our ₹0.38 is already well below typical market ask, and ₹0.35 is the proven floor we pay elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹10.19 L cash for us; if we can push to 15 days sooner (30 days), another ₹5.10 L comes free.

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit, or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.24 Cr annual spend is real money to a private packaging converter, but without their numbers we can't measure how much. The play here is to anchor hard on the ₹0.35/NOS price Premier delivers, line up one of the big alternates (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) as a credible second source, and use the threat of a split buy to get both the price match and faster payment.

evidence.point: Premier Plastic sells us the identical 30mm measuring cup for less
Closing that gap saves us real money
Switching to 30-day payment frees up cash we can use elsewhere
The open market asking price for a similar PP cap is much higher than what we pay
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc typical ask, vs our ₹0.38; verdict: MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume

evidence.point: We spend a meaningful amount with Mars each year

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — with ₹2569.83 Cr revenue and a B health score (65/100); the top second-source candidate to split this business

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) at ₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B (73/100) — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer with pan-India presence, medium confidence

risks: Mars has no public financials, so we're flying blind on their financial strength — if they're fragile, pushing too hard on price and payment together could backfire.
We already pay ₹0.38/NOS, which is well below the typical market ask of ₹0.85–0.95/pc — Mars may argue they're already giving us a great deal and have little room to move.
If we split the business to Manjushree or Mold-Tek without a trial, we take on qualification risk and potential supply hiccups during the switch.
The 45-day terms aren't our worst in the book, so Mars may resist cutting 15 days unless we sweeten the deal (bigger volume commitment or longer contract).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about matching the ₹0.35 price Premier gives us on the same measuring cup, and moving to 30-day payment so we can keep growing this business with you.
